pages.title: Talking to an Elder
text: Every tribe's camp has an **Elder**, and once you are a Guest they will talk to you. Right-click one and a conversation opens: what they say on the left, what you can say back as buttons.

Trading is one of the things you can ask for; it is the same counter as before, just behind a question. Strangers only get a few gruff words and a hint about the hearth, so bring an offering first (see [Tribes and standing](standing)).
What the Elder offers changes with what you have done: requests, their story, and once you have finished it, a warmer welcome.

pages.title: Requests
text: Ask an Elder **"Is there work I can do?"** and they give you one of the tribe's requests: fetch something they prize, deliver their dish cooked, turn back a few of the dark's creatures near their fires, perform a rite at a brazier in their camp, or raise a small build with Builder's Chalk in hand.
Each tribe has three requests open on any given day, and they change with the days, so if today's does not suit you, come back tomorrow. You hold **one request per tribe** at a time.

Finish it and tell the Elder **"I've done what you asked."** Each pays standing (8 to 16, before any camp bonuses), and every **third** finished request for a tribe pays a **Tribe Mark** on top, so you no longer have to wait for Voice to hold one.
The Codex keeps track for you: every tribe's page ends with their open request and how far along it is.

pages.title: Their story
text: Ask **"Tell me your story"** and the Elder begins a longer road: **seven steps**, one tribe at a time, that lean on everything else you do with them. Become their Friend, bring the one thing they prize, hunt near their fires, perform a rite in their camp, cook their dish, and at the end go where they send you.

The last step is a **trial**: each tribe's country keeps a guardian, and the tribe wants it faced. The Loom-stitchers' trial is The Unsung itself; the other eight wait at their grounds, told in [The guardians](guardians). Fall in the fight and nothing is lost: call it again when the altar has rested.

Finish the story and the Elder hands you the tribe's **relic**: a small, unique thing that grants that tribe's [boon](tribe_boons) whenever it is in your inventory, whatever your standing, and marks you for good in their eyes.

pages.title: The nine relics
text: {item:tribalpower:relic_soil} **Kept Ember** (Pad-keepers). {item:tribalpower:relic_stone} **Ringing Stone** (Grit-singers). {item:tribalpower:relic_sprout} **First Root** (Rootbinders). {item:tribalpower:relic_claw} **Bridge Nail** (Edge-walkers). {item:tribalpower:relic_spark} **Steady Drum** (Drumhearts). {item:tribalpower:relic_clock} **Silent Gear** (Pattern-weavers). {item:tribalpower:relic_swarm} **Hive Seal** (Colony-keepers). {item:tribalpower:relic_sigil} **Polite Seal** (Seal-carvers). {item:tribalpower:relic_spindle} **Ninth Thread** (Loom-stitchers).
One for each tribe, each the end of a story and the start of nine agreeing again.
